calls.head: Who drives the play: the Wild
calls.body: The Wild have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Canucks the worst. Expect the Wild to spend more of the night in the Canucks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 72% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Minnesota brought the hits
surprises.body: Minnesota’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 211, against their usual 95 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 300 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Minnesota picked Vancouver’s defense apart
surprises.body: Vancouver usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Minnesota’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.8% against Vancouver) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Hughes reaches 500 points as the Wild beat the Canucks
paras: Maxim Shabanov struck first for the Wild on the power play late in the first, and Bobby Brink made it 2-0 early in the second. The Canucks went more than 19 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the second to early in the third, while the Wild put 19 on net. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. Quinn Hughes stretched the lead to 3-0 on the power play midway through the second, his 500th NHL point, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Kirill Kaprizov made it 4-0 early in the third, but Max Sasson got the Canucks on the board less than three minutes later. Brock Boeser cut Minnesota’s lead to 4-2 with just over three minutes left.

The Wild dominated, and the replays agree: run this game’s chances back a hundred times and the Wild win about four in five. Calvin Pickard made 15 saves for the Wild, and Leevi Meriläinen, who gave up five goals against Carolina in his last start, kept the Canucks in it, stopping 30 of 34. The Wild improved to 8-3-2, climbing into first in the Central. The Canucks are still last in the NHL. The Canucks are winless in ten (0-9-1).

items.text: Joel Eriksson Ek passed Zach Parise for a tie for tenth on the Wild’s all-time assists list, with 202.
Kirill Kaprizov scored again against Vancouver, and has six goals in nine games against them since 2023-24.
Bobby Brink scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 21 (20 games played since).
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
